text:
Mia Lopez: Quick sync — we need a decision on streaming semantics for chat/completions before next sprint. Main tradeoffs: SSE vs WebSocket, delta shape (token-level vs chunked events), and canonical finish reasons. Customers pushing for tool-calling and mid-stream signals. Any blockers?

Arjun Rao: Can you list constraints we must satisfy? latency targets, SDK support, infra limits, and enterprise proxies?

Mia Lopez: Sure — baseline: first-token latency <200ms for hosted; JS + Python SDKs must support streaming; enterprise customers often sit behind proxies/firewalls that block WS. Also need clear finish_reason taxonomy for analytics and fallbacks.

Kevin Müller: From runtime side: we can emit token-by-token or emit chunked "delta" events that group tokens + control messages. Token-by-token is higher event rate and CPU overhead. Chunked deltas look like:```
{ "type": "delta", "role": "assistant", "content": "..." }
{ "type": "tool", "name": "search", "payload": "..." }
{ "type": "done", "reason": "stop" }
```
Chunked makes batching easier and reduces NEtwork chatter.

Olivia Chen: SDK perspective: SSE is easiest for browsers (EventSource) and works through many proxies, but it's unidirectional (server->client). WebSocket gives bidirectional so you can push client responses back on same connection which helps interactive tool flows. But browsers+mobile handle WS fine too, and our SDKs can polyfill.

Samir Patel: Customer ask: one enterprise asked for server-initiated tool invocation mid-stream (e.g., model calls a retriever, then asks client to confirm). That implies either: 1) server emits a tool_call event and client then does an additional HTTP call to complete, or 2) use WS so client can respond inline on stream. Which is higher priority?

Mia Lopez: For v1 we can require client to make an HTTP call back when tool input is needed. That keeps streaming protocol one-way. So SSE is viable. But we must surface clear events so clients can programmatically detect tool_call and present UI.

Arjun Rao: Agree with approach. Proposal: default streaming protocol = SSE (hosted + private). Offer WebSocket as opt-in for customers wanting lower-latency bidirectional interactions and long-lived sessions. Implementation notes:
- Server emits event types: `delta`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `done`
- Each event includes a `seq` field so clients can reassemble reliably
- `delta` payload can be either `text` or `structured` for function/tool call tokens

Kevin Müller: Implementation cost: SSE path leverages existing HTTP stack, less infra churn. WS requires connection manager, auth refresh, and scaling work. We can scope WS to Dedicated/Private first.

Olivia Chen: SDKs: we'll implement streaming helper that normalizes both transports into a single event stream for users. For JS we expose an async iterator that yields {type, content, seq}. For Python the same with iterator/generator. Migration guide required.

Mia Lopez: Finish_reason taxonomy proposal (must be stable): `stop` (normal end), `length` (hit max tokens), `cancel` (user/caller canceled), `tool_call` (stream paused to await tool input), `error` (runtime failure). These should be explicit in `done` event:```
{ "type": "done", "reason": "length" }
```

Samir Patel: Launch criteria for v1 streaming:
1) Hosted SSE streaming in JS + Python SDKs with examples
2) chunked `delta` event shape + documented event types
3) finish_reason set implemented and surfaced in console metrics
4) Migration doc + server-side toggles for WS opt-in
5) Integration test with a customer scenario (tool_call -> client HTTP callback)

Mia Lopez: Prioritization: aim for alpha next sprint (2 weeks) with SSE-only + SDK primitives. WS tracked as a separate initiative for Dedicated.

Kevin Müller: Test plan: load test token-rate with chunked deltas, simulate enterprise proxies, test reorder/retry using `seq` field. Also validate that tooling (reconnect semantics) can resume correctly or fall back to non-stream mode.

Arjun Rao: Security/observability: make sure tool_call events don't leak sensitive payloads. All events must respect customer KMS/HSM rules when Private. Tracing: include trace_id in every event header.

stream-bot: deploy:staging streaming-sse v1 deployed to canary cluster at 2026-03-10T15:12Z :rocket:

Mia Lopez: Next steps: (1) Accept the SSE-first + chunked-delta proposal? (2) Approve finish_reason list? (3) Assign owners for SDK work and infra canary? Please react or reply.

Olivia Chen: +1 to SSE-first, will take SDK owner.

Arjun Rao: +1, I'll own infra canary and sequencing.

Kevin Müller: +1, I'll do runtime chunking and seq fields.

Samir Patel: +1, documenting and customer comms on me.

Mia Lopez: Great — locking decision. We'll open a spec PR with these details and the launch checklist. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
